# A work identified by its DOI, shared by every reader who cites it. Readers'
# own annotations stay on their notes. Its metadata, and the state of the latest
# request for it, are shared too.
class Citation < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :notes, foreign_key: :citation_doi

  enum :enrichment_status, { pending: 0, completed: 1, failed: 2 }, prefix: :enrichment

  validates :doi, format: { with: %r{\A10\.\d{4,9}/\S+\z} }

  # Marks the citation pending and queues a metadata lookup, unless one is
  # already pending. Returns whether a lookup was queued. The job is queued under
  # the row lock, so a failed enqueue rolls back the pending state.
  def request_enrichment
    with_lock do
      if enrichment_pending?
        false
      else
        update!(enrichment_status: :pending, enrichment_error: nil)
        CitationEnrichmentJob.perform_later(self)
        true
      end
    end
  end

  # Asks the provider for this DOI's metadata. A permanent refusal marks the
  # enrichment failed; an unavailable provider raises so the job can retry.
  def enrich
    metadata = Provider.new.lookup(doi)
    record_enrichment(title: metadata.title, source_url: metadata.source_url, enrichment_status: :completed, enrichment_error: nil)
  rescue Provider::Error => error
    fail_enrichment(error.message)
  end

  def fail_enrichment(reason)
    record_enrichment(enrichment_status: :failed, enrichment_error: reason)
  end

  private
    # The job can load this citation before the request that queued it commits.
    # Taking the row lock waits for that commit and reloads, so the result is
    # written even when it equals the values loaded earlier.
    def record_enrichment(attributes)
      with_lock { update!(attributes) }
    end
end
# A Markdown file of one notebook's notes, written by ExportJob. The reader can
# cancel it while it is queued or working; the worker checks between notes and
# stops. A completed file can be downloaded until it expires.
class Export < ApplicationRecord
  AVAILABLE_FOR = 24.hours

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, { queued: 0, working: 1, completed: 2, cancelled: 3 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def cancellable?
    queued? || working?
  end

  # Cancels a queued or working export. Returns whether it was cancelled.
  def cancel
    with_lock do
      if cancellable?
        update!(status: :cancelled)
      else
        false
      end
    end
  end

  # Writes the notebook's notes, oldest first, under its export heading. Progress
  # is saved after each note. A cancelled export stops before the next note and
  # keeps no file.
  def generate
    notes = notebook.notes.with_rich_text_body.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    return unless start(notes.size)

    fragments = ["# #{notebook.export_heading || notebook.name}\n"]
    notes.each_with_index do |note, index|
      fragments << markdown_for(note)
      return unless record_progress(index + 1)
    end

    finish(fragments.sum)
  end

  # The authoritative check for downloading the file.
  def downloadable?
    completed? && expires_at.future?
  end

  private
    # A retried job starts again from the first note.
    def start(total)
      with_lock do
        update!(status: :working, processed_notes_count: 0, total_notes_count: total) if cancellable?
      end
    end

    def record_progress(count)
      with_lock do
        update!(processed_notes_count: count) unless cancelled?
      end
    end

    # The file is stored before the export is marked completed, so a completed
    # export always has one.
    def finish(markdown)
      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new(markdown),
        filename: "#{notebook.slug}.md", content_type: "text/markdown")

      completed = with_lock do
        update!(file: blob, status: :completed, expires_at: AVAILABLE_FOR.from_now) unless cancelled?
      end

      blob.purge unless completed
    end

    def markdown_for(note)
      body = note.body.to_plain_text.strip
      markdown = "\n## #{note.title.squish}\n"
      markdown += "\n#{body}\n" if body.present?
      markdown
    end
end
require "csv"

# A CSV of notes for one notebook. A preview reads and validates the rows without
# saving anything. Applying validates them again and saves the import with every
# row's note, or saves nothing.
class Import < ApplicationRecord
  HEADERS = %w[ title body_html doi annotation reminder_epoch ]
  MAXIMUM_SIZE = 100.kilobytes
  MAXIMUM_ROWS = 100

  Row = Struct.new(:line, :note, :annotation)

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_many :notes, dependent: :nullify

  validate :csv_is_importable, on: :create

  # Reads one byte past the limit, which is enough to reject a larger file.
  def file=(upload)
    self.csv = String.new(upload.read(MAXIMUM_SIZE + 1).to_s, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
  end

  def csv
    @csv.to_s
  end

  def csv=(text)
    @csv = text.to_s
    @rows = nil
  end

  def rows
    parse unless @rows
    @rows
  end

  # The reader's annotations by source line.
  def annotations
    rows.each_with_object(ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess.new) do |row, annotations|
      annotations[row.line] = row.annotation
    end
  end

  # Validates the file and every row without saving. Returns whether the import
  # can be applied, leaving the errors on the import and each row's note.
  def preview
    valid? && rows.map { |row| row.note.valid? }.all?
  end

  def apply
    return false if invalid?

    transaction do
      save!
      rows.each do |row|
        return false unless row.note.save
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def receipt
    CSV.generate do |csv|
      csv << %w[ title doi ]
      notes.includes(:citation).order(:id).each do |note|
        citation = note.citation
        csv << [ note.title, citation && citation[:id] ]
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def parse
      @rows, @headers, @problem = [], nil, nil
      return if csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE || !csv.valid_encoding?

      reader = CSV.new(csv.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").encode(universal_newline: true))
      citations = {}
      next_line = 1

      reader.each do |fields|
        line, next_line = next_line, next_line + reader.line.count("\n")

        if @headers.nil?
          @headers = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
          break if @headers != HEADERS
        elsif fields.size != HEADERS.size && fields.any?
          @problem = "line #{line} has #{fields.size} fields instead of #{HEADERS.size}"
          break
        elsif fields.any?
          @rows << build_row(line, fields, citations)
          break if @rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        end
      end
    rescue CSV::MalformedCSVError => error
      @problem = "it is not valid CSV (#{error.message})"
    end

    # Rows naming the same DOI share one citation, so it is created only once.
    def build_row(line, fields, citations)
      title, body_html, doi, annotation, reminder_epoch = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
      citation = citations[doi] ||= Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?

      note = Note.new(notebook: notebook, import: self, title: title, body: body_html, citation: citation,
        annotation: annotation.presence, reminder_epoch: reminder_epoch.presence)

      Row.new(line, note, annotation.presence)
    end

    def csv_is_importable
      rows

      if csv.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, :blank)
      elsif csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE
        errors.add(:csv, "must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_SIZE)} or smaller")
      elsif !csv.valid_encoding?
        errors.add(:csv, "must be UTF-8 text")
      elsif @problem
        errors.add(:csv, "cannot be read because #{@problem}")
      elsif @headers != HEADERS
        errors.add(:csv, "must start with the header row #{HEADERS.join(",")}")
      elsif rows.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain at least one note")
      elsif rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain #{MAXIMUM_ROWS} notes or fewer")
      end
    end
end
class Note < ApplicationRecord
  HIGHLIGHT_COLORS = %w[ yellow green blue pink ]
  MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE = 1.megabyte

  belongs_to :notebook
  belongs_to :import, optional: true
  belongs_to :citation, optional: true, foreign_key: :citation_doi, validate: true
  has_rich_text :body

  enum status: { draft: 0, ready: 1 }, _prefix: true

  serialize :tags, JSON
  store_accessor :settings, :color
  alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :color, inclusion: { in: HIGHLIGHT_COLORS }, allow_blank: true
  validates :reminder_epoch, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0, less_than: 10_000_000_000 }, allow_nil: true
  validate :attachments_are_small

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :titled_like, ->(query) { where("notes.title ILIKE ?", "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query)}%") }

  def doi
    citation_doi
  end

  # Cites the shared citation with this exact DOI, ignoring surrounding whitespace.
  # A blank DOI removes the citation from the note.
  def doi=(doi)
    doi = doi.to_s.strip
    self.citation = (Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?)
  end

  # The reminder time in the reader's time zone.
  def reminder_at
    Time.find_zone!(notebook.user.time_zone).at(reminder_epoch) if reminder_epoch
  end

  # Twenty-four elapsed hours after the reminder time, for postponing it a day.
  # The result keeps the reminder's UTC offset, so across a daylight saving
  # change its wall-clock time differs from the reader's local time.
  def next_day_reminder_at
    reminder_at.to_time + 86_400
  end

  def reminder_scheduled?
    reminder_job_id.present? && reminder_sent_at.nil?
  end

  # Schedules an email reminder at the given time in seconds since 1970, by
  # default the stored one, such as an imported reminder. It replaces any
  # earlier reminder for this note: the earlier job sends nothing when it runs.
  # Returns whether the reminder was scheduled. The job is queued under the row
  # lock, so a failed enqueue leaves the previous reminder in place.
  def schedule_reminder(epoch = reminder_epoch)
    with_lock do
      self.reminder_epoch = epoch

      if reminder_epoch && valid?
        job = NoteReminderJob.set(wait_until: reminder_epoch).perform_later(self)
        update!(reminder_job_id: job.job_id, reminder_sent_at: nil)
      else
        errors.add(:base, "Choose a date and time for the reminder") if reminder_epoch.nil?
        restore_attributes([:reminder_epoch])
        false
      end
    end
  end

  def postpone_reminder
    reminder_scheduled? && schedule_reminder(next_day_reminder_at.to_i)
  end

  # Sends the reminder if the given job is still the one scheduled for it.
  # Taking the row lock waits for the request that queued the job to commit.
  def send_reminder(job_id)
    with_lock do
      if reminder_job_id == job_id && reminder_scheduled?
        update!(reminder_sent_at: Time.current)
        ReminderMailer.with(note: self).note_reminder.deliver_now
      end
    end
  end

  def tag_list
    tags.join(", ")
  end

  def tag_list=(list)
    self.tags = list.to_s.split(",").map(&:strip).reject(&:blank?).uniq
  end

  private
    def attachments_are_small
      if body.body&.attachables.to_a.grep(ActiveStorage::Blob).any? { |blob| blob.byte_size > MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE }
        errors.add(:body, "attachments must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE)} or smaller")
      end
    end
end
class Notebook < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :user
  has_many :notes, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :imports, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :exports, dependent: :destroy

  serialize :preferences
  attr_readonly :slug

  before_validation :assign_slug, on: :create

  validates :name, presence: true

  def export_heading
    preferences.to_h["export_heading"]
  end

  def export_heading=(heading)
    self.preferences = preferences.to_h.merge("export_heading" => heading.to_s.strip.presence).compact
  end

  # Queues a Markdown export. The export is saved before its job is queued, so
  # the worker can always load it, and removed again if Redis refuses the job.
  def request_export
    export = exports.create!
    export.update!(job_id: ExportJob.perform_async(export.id, { format: "markdown" }))
    export
  rescue Redis::BaseError
    export&.destroy
    raise
  end

  # The number of notes, in any status, created on each UTC date, newest date
  # first, as [date, count] pairs. Dates without notes are omitted. Only notes
  # that still exist are counted, so deleting a note lowers its date's count.
  # Timestamps are stored in UTC, so their date part is the UTC date. The raw
  # select returns that date as PostgreSQL's ISO 8601 text.
  def daily_note_counts
    days = notes.select("DATE(notes.created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS notes_count").group("day").order("day DESC")
    Note.connection.select_rows(days).map { |day, count| [Date.iso8601(day), count] }
  end

  private
    def assign_slug
      self.slug = name.to_s.parameterize.presence || "notebook"
    end
end
class User < ApplicationRecord
  # Keep digest reservations past the end of their UTC day.
  DIGEST_RESERVATIONS_KEPT_FOR = 2.days

  has_secure_password

  has_many :notebooks, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :notes, through: :notebooks

  before_validation { self.email = email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :time_zone, inclusion: { in: ActiveSupport::TimeZone.all.map(&:name) }

  def self.authenticate(email, password)
    find_by(email: email.to_s.strip.downcase)&.authenticate(password)
  end

  # Reads a date and time the reader entered, such as "2026-10-31T09:00", in
  # their time zone. Returns nil when it is blank or not a valid time.
  def local_time(text)
    Time.find_zone!(time_zone).iso8601(text.to_s) if text.present?
  rescue ArgumentError
    nil

  # Queues an email digest of ready notes updated today (UTC), unless the reader
  # has already requested one for that UTC day. Returns whether a digest was queued.
  #
  # A Redis set of reader IDs for each day holds the reservations. If the job
  # cannot be queued, the reservation is released and the error raised, so the
  # reader can ask again. This prevents repeated requests, not repeated

  # Lists the reader's ready notes last updated on the day of the request.
  # Active Job deserializes the request time in the worker's time zone (UTC),
  # so that is the day the digest covers, which can differ from the reader's

  def daily_digest

    @date = requested_at.to_date
    @notes = @reader.notes.status_ready.where(updated_at: requested_at.all_day).includes(:notebook).order(:updated_at, :id)
    @completion = BigDecimal(params[:completion])

    mail to: @reader.email, subject: "Your reading digest for #{l @date, format: :long}"
  end
end

# Rails 7.0.8.7 → 8.1.0: upgrade risk for Margin Notes

The upgrade carries five high-risk changes, three of them in Active Job. Most are quiet changes in how jobs, times and cached pages behave, and several only show up in a Sidekiq worker or in production. Eight more changes raise errors with simple fixes, most of them at boot.

## Facts the ratings depend on (please correct any that are wrong)
- **PostgreSQL** only (`config/database.yml`). MySQL and SQLite changes are not relevant.
- **`config.load_defaults 7.0` stays as it is** (`config/application.rb:12`). I rated against the 7.0 defaults, so 7.1–8.1 defaults like `enqueue_after_transaction_commit`, `postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`, the HTML5 sanitizer and `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time` stay off. Adopting any of them later is a separate decision.
- **Active Job runs on Sidekiq 6.5.12 with redis 4.8.1** (`config/application.rb:21`), and Sidekiq jobs are also used directly (`ExportJob`). Tests use the Active Job test adapter.
- **Full-stack HTML app**: Sprockets, importmap, Turbo, Action Text and Active Storage on the Disk service. `ExportJob` writes Markdown files.
- **No cache store is set**, so production uses Rails' default file store. Fragment caching is used in `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26`.
- **What else moves**: I resolved the dependencies in `/tmp/res` with only the Rails pin changed. Only the Rails gems move, plus some small new ones (action_text-trix, rackup, rack-session, useragent, securerandom, bigdecimal 4.1.3, json, uri). Rack stays 2.2, and Sidekiq, Redis, Puma, Pagy and Faraday don't change (from the resolution I ran).
- Ruby 3.3.6 meets Rails 8's requirement of 3.2 or newer.

## High risk

**1. `retry_on wait: :exponentially_longer` no longer works, and failed lookups stay "pending" forever**
- **Before:** deprecated in 7.1, it worked as the polynomial backoff.
- **Now:** 8.1 `determine_delay` only knows `:polynomially_longer` and raises `"Couldn't determine a delay..."` for anything else (code read: `activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/exceptions.rb:175-187`).
- **Where:** `app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`.
- **What goes wrong:** it boots fine. The error only appears in the worker, the first time the provider is unavailable. The `retry_on` block never runs, so `fail_enrichment` is never called and the citation stays `pending`. `Citation#request_enrichment` (`app/models/citation.rb:16`) then refuses every new request for that DOI. Sidekiq's own retries just hit the same error again (inference).
- **Fix:** change it to `:polynomially_longer`.
- **Source:** activejob CHANGELOG for 7.1 (deprecation) and 7.2 (removal): https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md and https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md

**2. `DigestJob` now gets the time in the reader's time zone, which changes which day the digest covers**
- **Before:** 7.0's `TimeWithZoneSerializer#deserialize` did `Time.iso8601(value).in_time_zone`, which gave the worker's zone (UTC).
- **Now:** 8.1 stores the zone along with the time and restores it: `.in_time_zone(hash["time_zone"] || Time.zone)` (code read, `activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/serializers/time_with_zone_serializer.rb:16`).
- **Where:** `app/models/user.rb:34` builds `requested_at` in the reader's zone, and line 41 queues it. `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:3-9` relies on getting UTC: its comment says so, and it uses `requested_at.to_date` and `requested_at.all_day`.
- **What goes wrong:** the digest silently switches to the reader's local day. It picks different notes and shows a different date in the subject. Meanwhile the Redis reservation key is still based on the UTC day (inference).
- **Jobs queued before the upgrade** have no zone stored, so they keep the old UTC behaviour.

**3. `DigestJob`'s completion number is stored in a new format, which breaks jobs while old and new versions run side by side**
- **Before:** in 7.0, `BigDecimal` went to Sidekiq as-is and came back as a string.
- **Now:** 8.1 runs it through `BigDecimalSerializer`, which writes `{"_aj_serialized" => ...}` (code read, `activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/serializers.rb:107`, `arguments.rb:40`).
- **Where:** the call site is `app/models/user.rb:41`.
- **What goes wrong:** the new code itself is fine, because `BigDecimal(BigDecimal)` works in `digest_mailer.rb:9`. But during a rolling deploy, a 7.0 worker that picks up a job queued by 8.1 raises `DeserializationError`, and that digest is lost (inference).

**4. Export Markdown output changes for some rich text**
- **What changed:** `to_plain_text` was rewritten (code diff of `action_text/plain_text_conversion.rb`).
  - Ordered-list numbers are now counted over elements only. Before, whitespace text nodes were counted too, which can shift the numbers.
  - The contents of `<script>` and `<style>` are now dropped.
- **Where:** `app/models/export.rb:78`, `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:53` and `app/views/imports/preview.html.erb:58`.
- **Impact:** it is a correction, so the practical risk is small, but generated files will differ from earlier exports (inference).

**5. Expired exports are now cached with no expiry**
- **Before:** 7.0 wrote the entry with an expiry already in the past, so it was never served.
- **Now:** when the expiry is negative, 8.1 logs an error and drops `expires_in` (code read, `activesupport-8.1.0/lib/active_support/cache.rb:922-944`; it only raises if the 7.1+ default is turned on).
- **Where:** `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26` passes `expires_in: export.expires_at - Time.current`, which is negative once an export has expired.
- **What goes wrong:** the "Expired" fragment is stored with no expiry. The page still shows the right thing, because the export stays expired. But the file store keeps those entries forever and the logs fill with errors (inference).
- **Fix:** skip caching or clamp the value when it is 0 or less.

## Medium risk

- **The Rails-provided Sidekiq adapter is deprecated and will be removed in 8.2.** 8.1 warns: "upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later" (code read, `activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/queue_adapters/sidekiq_adapter.rb:33-37`). Moving to Sidekiq 7 is a decision in itself:
  - It drops the `redis` gem in favour of `redis-client`.
  - `redis.sadd(key, id)` then returns an Integer (always truthy) instead of true/false. That would break the one-digest-per-day check in `app/models/user.rb:38` without any error (inference).
  - `rescue Redis::BaseError` in `app/models/notebook.rb:28` would stop catching Redis errors (inference).
- **`to_time_preserves_timezone` is deprecated and will be removed in 8.2.** `load_defaults 7.0` sets it, so expect deprecation warnings (code read, `activesupport-8.1.0/lib/active_support.rb:124-136`). `TimeWithZone#to_time` now always keeps the zone. `Note#next_day_reminder_at` (`app/models/note.rb:46`) gives the same `.to_i`, so reminders don't move, but the comment at line 44 becomes inaccurate (inference).

## Low risk (each one raises an error with a simple fix)

These were confirmed by reading the 8.1 source. Most fail at boot, under eager load, or in the tests. The two that only fail when that code runs are marked.

- **`enum status: {...}, _prefix: true`** (`app/models/note.rb:10`): keyword-style `enum` was removed in 8.0. Use `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true`.
- **`serialize :tags, JSON`** (`app/models/note.rb:12`): passing the coder by position was removed in 7.2. Use `coder: JSON`. `serialize :preferences` (`notebook.rb:7`) keeps YAML under the 7.0 defaults.
- **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`** (`app/models/note.rb:14`): `color` is a `store_accessor`, not a column, and 8.1 raises `ArgumentError` (`attribute_methods.rb:90`). Use `alias_method` for the reader and the writer. This is used by the form, the controller params and the views.
- **`set(wait_until: <Integer>)`** (`app/models/note.rb:61`): 7.0 called `.to_f`, but 8.1 stores the value as-is and then calls `scheduled_at.utc` while serializing, which raises `NoMethodError`. Use `Time.at(reminder_epoch)`. This only fails when someone schedules a reminder.
- **`citation[:id]`** (`app/models/import.rb:68`): 7.0 mapped `"id"` to the primary key (`doi`), but 7.1+ no longer does, so the call raises `MissingAttributeError`. Use `citation.id` or `citation.doi`. This only fails on the receipt CSV download (covered by `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb`).
- **`get "/notes", "/journal", to:`** (`config/routes.rb:18`): more than one path in a single route now raises `ArgumentError` (`mapper.rb:1854`). Split it into two `get` lines.
- **`ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags += ...`** (`config/initializers/action_text.rb:1`): `allowed_tags` now starts as `nil`, so `+=` raises at boot. Build the list from `sanitizer.class.allowed_tags` and the Action Text tags yourself.
- **`Note.connection`** (`app/models/notebook.rb:40`): this is a quiet deprecation in 7.2+. `with_connection`/`lease_connection` are preferred.

## Judged not relevant

- **MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy adapters**: the app uses PostgreSQL.
- **PostgreSQL date decoding** (`decode_dates`): it is only turned on by the 7.1+ defaults, so `Date.iso8601(day)` in `notebook.rb:40` still gets strings.
- **`enqueue_after_transaction_commit`**: it defaults to false under the 7.0 defaults, so enqueuing inside `with_lock` still rolls back on failure as the code expects (code read, `enqueuing.rb:53`).
- **Rack 3, `:unprocessable_entity` and Puma**: Rack stays 2.2.
- **Solid Queue, Cache and Cable, Propshaft, Kamal and the auth generator**: these are new-app defaults and are not adopted.
- **Action Cable, Action Mailbox and Active Storage variants**: they are unused (no channels with code, no mailbox, no image_processing).
- **Cache format version**: 7.0 is still supported in 8.1.
- **Composite primary keys and other new 7.1–8.1 features**: they are opt-in.

Most claims above come from reading the 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 gem source, unpacked in `/tmp/gems`. The "what goes wrong" parts are my inference. I did not open the individual pull requests, so the changelog links point to the per-version CHANGELOG files rather than specific PRs.
